text: Was the message transferred from a mark already on the eraser when A pressed it onto the paper?
Did the eraser make the message visible by removing something from the paper?
Was the message left by physically deforming the paper with pressure from the eraser?
Did material from the eraser itself remain on the paper in message-shaped strokes?
Did A use the eraser to apply a separate writing substance, such as ink or graphite, to the paper?
Did friction from the eraser cause the paper itself to change color, revealing the message?
Was the message already present on the paper in an invisible form before A used the eraser?
Was the message formed by holes or cut-away shapes in the paper?
Did the eraser chemically alter the paper itself to make the message visible?
Was the intended recipient supposed to interpret the sheet’s remaining blank as the message?
Did A use the eraser to operate or trigger another object or device that put the message on the paper?
Did A arrange the eraser or a light source so that the eraser’s shadow formed the message on the paper?
Did heat produced by using the eraser make the message appear on the sheet?
Was the intended message communicated through a smell associated with the paper?
Could the recipient read the message from the eraser’s position on the sheet while it remained there?
Was the message conveyed by a sound A made while using the eraser?
Did A use the eraser on another object, and did that action indirectly cause the message to appear on the blank sheet?
Was the other object a surface used for writing or drawing?
Did using the eraser on the other object cause that object to release or transfer something that later made the message appear on the paper?
Did using the eraser on the other object prompt a person to produce the message on the paper?

Did A rub the eraser against the other object?

Was the other object a human being?
Did the eraser physically touch the other object?
Did A use the eraser to move or reposition the other object, rather than to affect its surface?
Did contact between the eraser and the other object directly cause a physical event that led to the message being written on the paper?
Did contact with the eraser cause the other object to move or change its position?
Did the eraser’s contact complete or interrupt an electrical circuit?
Did contact with the eraser cause a mechanical part of the other object to move?
Did the moving mechanical part actuate a writing instrument that marked the paper?
Did the moving mechanical part cause the paper or another object to move before A made the message by hand?
Did the moving part physically jolt or startle A, causing A’s hand to make the message?
Did the moving part change what A could physically do next, for example by opening or unlocking access to something?
Did the moving part open or unlock a place containing the paper A used?
Did the moving part open or unlock access to an item A then used to make the message?

Did the newly accessible item itself physically produce the message on the paper?
Was the newly accessible item necessary for A to make the message?
Was the newly accessible item a key?

Did A use the newly accessible item directly on the paper as part of creating the message?
Was the message communicated by the paper’s final shape or arrangement, rather than by marks on its surface?
Did A use the newly accessible item to guide or shape marks made by A, rather than to imprint them?
Did the newly accessible item make the message by exposing or burning the paper with light?
Did the newly accessible item leave visible marks by cutting, scratching, or puncturing the paper?
Did A use the newly accessible item to manipulate or apply something else to the paper, rather than to make marks with the item itself?
Did A press the newly accessible item against the paper to form message-shaped indentations?
Was the message made partly with a conventional writing instrument and partly through A’s direct use of the newly accessible item?
Did A use the newly accessible item itself to make any of the visible marks, even though it was not a conventional writing instrument?
Did the item interact with the paper in a way that produced a visible message without leaving marks made by the item itself?
Was the newly accessible item used to hold or stabilize the paper while A wrote the message with a separate writing instrument?
Was the newly accessible item physically beneath the sheet while A made the message?
Was the newly accessible item an electronic device?
Did A use the newly accessible item to direct light through or onto the paper so that the light itself made the message visible?
Did A use the newly accessible item to fasten the paper to another object?
Did A place or arrange the newly accessible item itself on the paper to communicate the message, rather than use it to create marks?
Did A use the item to change the paper in a way that made the message readable only later or under special conditions?
Did A use the newly accessible item to fold or crease the sheet, with that fold or crease helping communicate the message?
Was the newly accessible item a liquid?
Did A use the newly accessible item to view or read something while making the message, rather than to alter the paper?
While A made the message’s visible marks by hand, was the newly accessible item in contact with the paper?
Was the newly accessible item a glove?
Was the newly accessible item in contact with the top face of the paper while A wrote the message?
Was the newly accessible item part of A’s body?
Did A rest their writing hand or wrist on the newly accessible item while writing?
Was the newly accessible item a sheet placed on top of the blank paper while A wrote?
Was the newly accessible item a surface or material that interacted with the separate writing instrument while A wrote?
Did the newly accessible item serve as a physical barrier or cover on the paper while A wrote, rather than making or shaping any marks?
Was the newly accessible item made primarily of paper or card, even though it was not a sheet placed on top of the blank page?
Did the item’s contact with the paper affect where the writing instrument could make marks, even though it did not itself shape or produce them?
Did the newly accessible item contain information that A copied into the message?
Did A use the newly accessible item to protect or treat the paper’s surface while writing?

Was the newly accessible item’s contact with the paper incidental to its main role in the scene?
Did the item’s contact with the paper serve a deliberate function while A wrote, even though it neither affected the marks nor supported the writing hand?
Did A write on the newly accessible item while it was in contact with the blank sheet?
Was the newly accessible item attached to the writing instrument while A wrote?
Did the newly accessible item’s function while attached to the writing instrument enable A to make the message?
Was the newly accessible item a pencil extender?
Was the newly accessible item a replaceable part, such as lead or a refill, that the writing instrument needed in order to write?
Was the newly accessible part a replaceable graphite lead for a pencil?
Was the newly accessible replacement lead stored inside the other object, rather than in a separate container that the object opened?
Was the other object itself a writing instrument, with the eraser moving a mechanism that opened its internal lead supply?
Was the other object itself a writing instrument?
Did A press the eraser against a mechanical part of the writing instrument to advance a replacement graphite lead out of it?
Did the eraser actuate a mechanism that opened the writing instrument’s lead-storage chamber?
Did the moving part release or expose a spare graphite lead without opening the lead-storage chamber or advancing lead through the pencil tip?
Did the eraser move a latch or cover on the writing instrument, rather than its lead-advancing mechanism?
Did the moving part release the replacement lead from an external holder or compartment on the writing instrument?
Did A insert the newly accessible lead into the writing instrument before writing the message?

A used the eraser to actuate a mechanical part of a writing instrument, which made a spare graphite lead accessible. A inserted the lead into the instrument and used it to write the message on the blank sheet.
Did the eraser-actuated part release a single spare lead from a holder on the writing instrument, which A then inserted?

A used the eraser to actuate a moving part of a writing instrument. That made a replacement graphite lead accessible, which A inserted into the instrument before using it to write the message. The clues do not establish exactly how the mechanism provided access to the lead.
